 Business Recorder • 16 Nov 2026, 6:34 AM PKT • 1 min read 
 ENG اردو A- A+ Add as preferred source on Google X f President Asif Ali Zardari has rejected the Federal Board of Revenue’s challenge to a recommendation that it introduce a Faceless Refund Regime, Business Recorder reported. The proposal would use Section 170A of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, to automate refund processing and send eligible amounts to taxpayers’ registered bank accounts.
 The case concerned a Rs42.86 million refund claim for tax year 2025, which remained pending. The order says refunds supported by tax credits confirmed through the Board’s computer system could be transferred without taxpayers filing formal refund applications. FBR had argued that the claim was still being verified and that an appeal route existed under Section 170(5); the decision maintained that administrative delay still required attention.
 Tax advisor Khurram Shahzad Butt told Business Recorder that an automated process could reduce delays and taxpayer contact with tax offices. He also cited Islamabad High Court directions seeking a mechanism under Section 170A, while FBR already operates faceless customs clearance and assessment systems.
 At a glance
 The president dismissed FBR’s challenge over the proposed refund regime.
 The pending claim involved Rs42.86 million for tax year 2025.
 Verified refunds could be transferred electronically without formal applications.
 Why it matters
 The decision concerns FBR’s income-tax refund administration and the proposed automation of payments to taxpayers.
